purpose: Fourth fresh generality batch, deliberately using frameworks and repositories not covered in batches 1-3: classic Flask blueprints, FastAPI multi-router applications, NestJS controllers, Rust Rocket fairing-mounted routes, a real Gin service/ORM application with response-envelope wrappers, Hono (native Fetch Response / redirect / custom error handler), and go-chi nested Route groups with Mount. Every project is pinned to a commit, scanned with an empty ledger and no project-specific rules, and expected routes were verified by reading the route registration source directly.

scoring.notes: Deterministic = provable from source. The only non-deterministic contracts in this batch are deliberate error-path routes whose response is produced by a registered framework error handler rather than the handler body: go-chi GET /panic panics into middleware.Recoverer (500), and Hono GET /error and GET /type-error funnel into app.onError (500). These are surfaced to the interactive AI gap review (response-unknown) rather than guessed, and are reported separately from deterministic completeness. Static file mounts, Swagger UI handlers and framework internals are not API operations and are excluded.

projects.baseline: Official Flask tutorial package: create_app adds GET /hello and the index alias; auth Blueprint (url_prefix /auth) exposes GET+POST /auth/register, GET+POST /auth/login, GET /auth/logout; blog Blueprint (no prefix) exposes GET /, GET+POST /create, GET+POST /<int:id>/update, POST /<int:id>/delete. 12 method-path operations; <int:id> maps to {id}.

Bigger Applications tutorial: GET /; users router GET /users/, GET /users/me, GET /users/{username}; items router (prefix /items) GET /items/, GET /items/{item_id}, PUT /items/{item_id}; internal admin router mounted at /admin with POST /admin/. 8 operations. GET /items returns a module-level literal table; GET /items/{item_id} indexes it and also raises HTTPException(404); PUT raises 403.
CatsController @Controller('cats'): POST /cats (void create -> empty 201), GET /cats (returns Promise<Cat[]>), GET /cats/:id (void findOne -> empty 200). 3 operations.

Three AdHoc fairing stages: json stage mounted at /json (POST /, PUT /{id}, GET /{id}), msgpack stage at /msgpack (POST /, GET /{id}), uuid stage at / (GET /people/<id>). 6 operations with format-derived JSON vs msgpack media types and 404 branches.

InitRouter: root POST /auth, POST /upload, and (registered on root r even inside the group block) POST /tags/export, POST /tags/import; apiv1 group /api/v1 exposes GET/POST /tags, PUT/DELETE /tags/:id, GET /articles, GET/POST /articles/:id handling plus GET /articles/:id, PUT/DELETE /articles/:id, POST /articles/poster/generate. StaticFS mounts and the gin-swagger /swagger/*any UI handler are not API operations. 14 operations, with 400/401/500/default envelope branches and ORM model payloads.

16 operations: GET /, /hello (native new Response(string)), /entry/:id, /redirect (c.redirect -> 302), /auth/*, /etag/cached, /fetch-url, /user-agent, /error (throws), /type-error (returns a non-Response), the /book route group (GET /, POST /, GET /:id), and /api routes (GET+POST /api/posts, GET /api/*). /error and /type-error produce their body via the registered app.onError (500) and are the interactive-AI exemplars for this batch.

Nested chi routers: GET /, /ping, /panic; /articles group with GET (paginated), POST, GET /search; /articles/{articleID} GET/PUT/DELETE; GET /articles/{articleSlug}; and Mount /admin with GET /admin/, GET /admin/accounts, GET /admin/users/{userId}. 13 operations. GET /panic only panics and relies on middleware.Recoverer for the 500, so it is the interactive-AI exemplar for this batch.
